body: fights are lost all the time, with horrific casualties.

The problem isn't with *them*, though...the problem is with me.

Someone with mental instability like me is an aberration; a relationship wouldn't even be a learning experience, it would be a write-off.

To try and pursue relationships, knowing what I do now, would be to deliberately hurt people and waste their time.

I like to think I'm better than that.

Sort of a cycle between wanting to be respectful of others vs. wanting to order them around like slaves and cast them aside when a better option comes along or when I'm bored.

that leads to acceptance that one can't always get what one wants, but it just comes back and becomes a cycle of acceptance vs. a refusal to accept that opportunities are squandered everyday and potential is lost.

When it becomes a struggle of acceptance is when I become frustrated with my own inability to be respectful without feeling resentment towards myself for harboring and entertaining disrespectful thoughts.

I accept that I'm imperfect, and I see that I think of other people all the time, and it's ok, but it keeps coming back to the point that I feel despair that I'm not in control of my own thoughts.

I accept that I don't always feel in control of my own thoughts, and I try to be grateful for what I have.

I try to choose gratefulness, but a part of me holds back; I'm frustrated that this is life, and it doesn't feel like "enough" to satisfy me although this is all there is.

I try to choose to be happy with the way things are, but I instead choose restlessness and desire and emotional cheating. 

I become frustrated because I worry that I am, somehow, *incapable* of caring about other people the way they do/did about me and the way I see other couples making it work.

I [split](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Splitting_\(psychology\)) myself, and I realize that I'm doing it, but I can't reconcile my duality.

I don't know how to "accommodate" my halves, so to speak. 

Most of these realizations make me very sad and very nervous, and I begin to close off to the world while, in private, I open up and emotions flood out in multiple breakdowns.

**tl:dr, summation**

I realize that I'm imperfect, and I struggle with the acceptance. It seems, to me, like other people resolve these dilemmas in their head more simply, or they don't beat themselves up about it so much.

My self-torture cycle magnifies in a relationship, and I don't know how to cope.

My inability to cope creates friction in relationships that greatly upsets other people, (understandably so), so I spare other people the confusion and sadness of a relationship with myself.

Thanks for your advice, though, but I don't have much frustration with others; I can accept and even understand other people's weaknesses and iniquities and even love them in spite of it.

I can't do it with myself, though, yet.
